nodes.name: Colloidal synthesis of NiCu NPs
nodes.procedure: The free-standing NiCu NPs with various compositions were synthesized by reducing Ni(acac)₂ and Cu(acac)₂ in oleylamine. In a typical synthesis of Ni₁Cu₁ NPs, 0.5 mmol Ni(acac)₂, 0.5 mmol Cu(acac)₂, 10 mL oleylamine, and 0.8 mL oleic acid were mixed at room temperature (25°C). The solution was then kept at 120°C under an Ar blanket for 30 min to remove the moisture. Then the solution was heated to 220°C at a heating rate of 2°C/min. The reaction was maintained at 220°C for 1 h and then naturally cooled down to room temperature. As-prepared Ni₁Cu₁ NPs were collected and washed by centrifugation. The composition was varied by changing the precursor ratio between Ni(acac)₂ and Cu(acac)₂.

nodes.name: Carbon loading of NiCu NPs
nodes.procedure: A suspension of Vulcan XC-72 (Premetek, U.S.A.) was prepared by sonicating ~320 mg of Vulcan in 600 mL hexane in an ice bath for 5 h. Afterward, a suspension of as-prepared NiCu NPs in hexane was added into the Vulcan suspension and the mixture was further sonicated for 2 additional hours. The catalyst powders were collected by purging Ar (evaporating hexane) at room temperature and dried in vacuum oven for 24 h. The mass loading of NiCu NPs at NiCu/C catalysts was controlled at 20 wt%.

nodes.name: Two-step heat treatment of NiCu/C
nodes.procedure: To remove the surfactants attached on NPs, the NiCu/C catalysts were heated up to 250°C under air and maintained at this temperature for 30 min. After naturally cooling down to the room temperature, the air atmosphere was switched to a mixture of H₂/Ar (5% H₂), and the temperature was further increased up to 200°C and maintained for 1 h.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiCu/C catalysts show spherical nanoparticles with comparable average particle sizes across different compositions, measured from >250 NPs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM shows that they are spherical (Figures 1 and S5-S9) without specific orientation... By counting >250 particles, the statistical average sizes of NiCu NPs (at NiCu/C after heat-treatment) are shown in Figure S3.

properties.description: Transmission Electron Microscopy image showing nanoparticles

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms fcc polycrystalline NiCu solid solution structure with diffraction peaks between Ni and Cu; after heat-treatment, NPs remain solid solutions with grain sizes from Scherrer analysis of (111) peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction patterns show typical fcc crystal phases with diffraction peaks between the standard Ni and Cu peaks... After this two-step heat-treatment, the XRD patterns confirm that the NPs are still solid solutions; and the grain sizes obtained from Scherrer equation analysis of XRD (111) peaks.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV determines electrochemical active surface area (ECSA): Ni ECSA from OH adsorption charge at 0.2 V vs RHE, Cu ECSA from Cu₂O monolayer formation charge at 0.6 V vs RHE; enables surface Ni coverage calculation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ECSA of Ni was extracted based on the Coulombic charge under the OH adsorption peak at 0.2 V vs RHE, and ECSA of Cu was measured by the charge under the peak (at 0.6 V vs RHE) which represents the formation of Cu₂O monolayer.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS valence band spectra determine d band center position as weight center after Shirley background correction; surface Ni fraction from Ni 2p (850-890 eV) and Cu 2p (925-960 eV) peak areas agrees with CV-ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Normalized valence band spectra (VBS) of various NiCu/C catalysts measured by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS)... Ni fraction derived from XPS agrees well with that obtained by ECSA.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP confirms bulk composition of NiCu NPs matches nominal precursor feeding ratios across all compositions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The consistency between the nominal feeding ratio of precursors and bulk composition ratio of NPs is confirmed by Inductively Coupled Plasma (ICP, Figure S4).
